scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - Bb - B - D
scalesUsed.application: Adds the blue note (Bb) for gritty, aggressive riff passages and bends

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D
scalesUsed.application: Defines the dominant tonality with the natural 3rd (G#) and flat 7th (D), used in chord voicings and melodic passages

keyAndScale.keySignature: 4 sharps (F#, C#, G#, D#) modified with b7 (D natural)

mainProgression.description: The iconic progression built around the 'Hendrix chord' (E7#9) with blues-rock power chord movement to G and A

sectionProgressions.description: The signature riff using the E7#9 chord with its clashing major 3rd and sharp 9th (minor 3rd), creating the song's psychedelic tension
Verse expands the main riff with vocal melody woven through the chord changes
Chromatic movement between F# and G creates dissonant tension before resolving back to E

harmonicFunction: E7#9 (I7#9) - The 'Hendrix chord' combines major and minor tonality, creating psychedelic ambiguity
G (bIII) - Borrowed from E minor, provides bluesy contrast and a dark harmonic pull
A (IV) - Subdominant movement delivering a momentary sense of resolution and lift
F# (II) - Used in chromatic passages to create tension against the bIII chord

techniques.name: The Hendrix Chord (E7#9)
techniques.description: The signature E7#9 voicing that defines the song's sound, combining a dominant 7th with a sharp 9th to create a chord that is simultaneously major and minor

notes: E7#9: 0-7-6-7-8-X (Hendrix voicing)
The #9 (G natural) clashes with the major 3rd (G#) in the chord
This chord is the foundation of Hendrix's psychedelic sound
Thumb wraps over the neck to fret the low E string
Requires stretching across multiple frets (6th to 8th)
sequence: Plant the thumb on the low E string (open or fretted)
Barre or place fingers across frets 6-8 on middle strings
Strike the chord with aggressive downstroke attack
Add rhythmic accents and muting between hits
tips: Mute the high E string to avoid unwanted noise
Use a punchy, aggressive attack for authenticity
Hendrix often used his thumb to fret bass notes while playing chords

techniques.name: Octave Riffs and Hammer-Ons
techniques.description: Hendrixthe iconic vocal hooks melodic riff passages between chord stabs

notes: Octave shapes played on E and D strings (2 strings apart, 2 frets up)
Hammer-ons from open strings to fretted notes for fluid riff movement
Combines single-note lines with chord stabs seamlessly
Uses fuzz-driven tone to blend notes together
sequence: Play the opening octave riff on the low strings
Hammer-on from open E to the fretted notes
Transition smoothly into the E7#9 chord stab
Repeat the riff pattern with rhythmic variations
tips: Practice hammer-ons with enough force for clear tone
Keep the fretting hand relaxed for quick movements
Mute unused strings with both hands to control noise
Use the fuzz pedal to help sustain hammer-on notes
details.progression: Octave riff leading into E7#9 - G - A

techniques.name: Psychedelic Lead Techniques
techniques.description: Hendrix's expressive lead playing combining fuzz tone, whammy bar dives, feedback, and aggressive bending for the solo sections

notes: Based in E minor pentatonic and blues scale positions
Heavy use of string bending (whole and 1.5 step bends)
Whammy bar manipulation for pitch dives and vibrato
Controlled feedback used as a musical element
Double stops and unison bends for thickness
sequence: Begin solo phrases with aggressive bends at the 12th fret
Incorporate whammy bar dips between phrases
Use feedback swells to transition between ideas
Build intensity through the solo section
tips: Crank the fuzz for authentic Hendrix solo tone
Practice controlled feedback by facing the amp
Study Hendrix's use of the whammy bar as an expressive tool
Focus on attitude and feel over technical precision

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: The iconic opening riff featuring the tritone interval (Bb to E) played with fuzz, establishing the song's psychedelic character immediately
notes: The opening uses the tritone interval (E to Bb) for dissonance
Heavy fuzz tone is essential for the sound
Hammer-ons create fluid movement between notes
This riff is one of the most recognizable in rock history

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Verse section built around the E7#9 chord stabs with rhythmic accents, creating a hypnotic groove under the vocal melody
notes: Aggressive E7#9 chord stabs with muted spaces between
Use thumb-over-neck technique for bass notes
Maintain tight rhythmic feel at 108 BPM
Let the fuzz tone create sustain and grit

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: A wild, fuzz-drenched guitar solo showcasing Hendrix's revolutionary approach to electric guitar with bends, whammy bar, and feedback
notes: Based in E minor pentatonic with blues scale additions
Aggressive bending and whammy bar use throughout
Controlled feedback adds to the psychedelic atmosphere
The solo builds in intensity and wildness

sections.name: Turnaround / Bridge
sections.description: The bridge section with chromatic movement between F# and G, creating dissonant tension before resolving back to the main riff
notes: Chromatic half-step movement creates tension
Power chord shapes moving up and down
Builds anticipation before the solo section
Keep the rhythm tight and aggressive

alternatives: Any Strat-style guitar with single coils and tremolo bar
guitar.pickup: Neck single-coil for warm lead tones, bridge pickup for aggressive riffs

effects.distortion: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face - germanium transistor fuzz, full gain
effects.other: Roger Mayer Octavia (octave fuzz) for solo sections; Uni-Vibe for rotary speaker effect on select passages

beginner.focus: Learn the basic power chord shapes and the main riff rhythm
steps: Learn E5, G5, and A5 power chord shapes
Practice the simplified main riff using power chords
Work on basic hammer-on technique from open strings
Develop steady rhythm at 108 BPM with metronome

intermediate.focus: Master the E7#9 chord voicing and authentic riff technique
steps: Learn the E7#9 (Hendrix chord) voicing with thumb-over-neck
Practice the full intro riff with octave shapes
Develop hammer-on/pull-off fluency for riff passages
Work on the verse chord progression with proper rhythmic feel

advanced.focus: Nail the guitar solo and develop Hendrix-style expressive techniques
steps: Develop fuzz pedal control and feedback technique
Master whammy bar techniques for pitch manipulation
Perform the complete song with all sections and dynamics

commonMistakes: Not fretting the E7#9 chord cleanly - practice the stretch slowly
Losing the rhythmic groove by focusing too much on chord shapes
Over-using effects to compensate for sloppy technique
Playing the riff too cleanly - Hendrix was raw and aggressive
practiceRoutine: Warm up with E minor pentatonic and blues scale runs (5 minutes)
Practice E7#9 chord voicing with clean transitions (10 minutes)
Work on the intro riff with fuzz at slow tempo (10 minutes)
Practice the solo section in short phrase segments (10 minutes)
Full song run-through with backing track (5 minutes)
focusAreas: E7#9 chord voicing and thumb-over-neck technique
Clean hammer-ons and pull-offs at tempo
Fuzz tone control and dynamic expression
metronomeWork: Start intro riff at 80 BPM, gradually increase to 108 BPM
Practice chord changes (E7#9 - G - A) at 90 BPM first
Solo phrasing: work at half speed focusing on bend accuracy
Full tempo run-through once comfortable with all sections
